title: XDLC: XRPL Dynamic Liquidity Corridors

status.label: Draft-Local (not submitted)
status.note: Proposed amendment drafted locally. Not submitted to XRPL-Standards, not reviewed, not implemented in xrpld, not activated on any network. The Titan Forge application-level corridor lifecycle is evidence of usefulness, not the amendment.

design: Neutral protocol: a corridor of provider liquidity pegged to an existing XRPL AMM that undercuts it by ImprovementBps at every depth level. Any organization can provide liquidity; GYW1313 (Titan Ghost, TG Intelligence) is one participant, off-ledger.

capabilities.name: AMM-pegged corridor liquidity
capabilities.summary: For a pair with an XLS-30 AMM, the payment engine synthesizes a corridor quote at the AMM's current spot quality (including its trading fee) improved by ImprovementBps (>= 1 bp), at every depth level. No repricing transactions, no directory entries for quotes, no oracle.

capabilities.name: Wallet-held commitments
capabilities.summary: Providers keep funds in their own accounts; a ledger hold makes committed funds unspendable by any other path (the accountHolds / xrpLiquid change). Flexible (Tier 1-like) or term (Tier 2-like).

capabilities.name: Activation-start terms
capabilities.summary: LockDuration starts when the corridor becomes ACTIVE, or at commit time if already ACTIVE. Before activation, withdrawal is free. Providers can join while FORMING or ACTIVE.

capabilities.name: Prorated early-exit fee to a tenure-weighted fee pool
capabilities.summary: fee = withdrawn x ExitFeeBps x remaining/term (fixed at commit, cap 1000 bps, rounded down), charged atomically in CorridorWithdraw, distributed to the providers who stay by tenure through an O(1) accumulator; claim on withdraw or via CorridorClaim.

capabilities.name: Tenure fill priority
capabilities.summary: At the same corridor level, commitments fill in (TenureStart, CommitmentID) order, bounded per step.

capabilities.name: Provider limits
capabilities.summary: Per commitment MinRate (base side) or MaxRate (Asset2 side) as the worst acceptable price, and MaxPerLevel; checked on executed amounts.

capabilities.name: Deterministic volatility pause
capabilities.summary: A corridor stops quoting while the AMM price deviates more than PauseBps from a reference taken from AMM state in an earlier ledger (one candidate per ledger, promoted in a later ledger).

capabilities.name: Optional permissioned providers
capabilities.summary: A corridor may reference a Permissioned Domain (XLS-80); only members may commit. Takers are not restricted (corridor quotes sit in the open book).

removedCapabilities.name: Group-funding threshold with automatic release
removedCapabilities.why: Commander decision: terms start at activation and exit is priced, not prohibited. Nothing is locked before activation, so there is nothing to release. An optional activation gate remains.

removedCapabilities.name: Operator-placed offers bounded by the participant
removedCapabilities.why: Corridor quotes are synthesized by the payment engine, so no operator places offers for providers. Bounded delegation, if ever needed, belongs to a general amendment.

candidateLedgerEntries.name: LiquidityCorridor
candidateLedgerEntries.reserve: one owner reserve (corridor owner); fee pools held by a corridor pseudo-account (AMM / Vault precedent)

candidateLedgerEntries.name: CorridorCommitment
candidateLedgerEntries.reserve: one owner reserve (provider); one per (corridor, account, asset)

amendmentNecessaryFor: G3 Liquidity that re-prices itself to the AMM at every depth (pegged / dynamic quotes)
G5 Self-custodial commitment: funds stay in the provider account but cannot be spent elsewhere
G6 Term commitment with a priced early exit (prorated fee) paid to the providers who stay
G7 Fill priority by tenure among providers at the same corridor level
G8 Provider-set limits on synthesized liquidity (worst price, max per depth level)
G9 Volatility guard without an oracle
G14 Lifecycle stage as consensus state
openQuestions: Volatility pause reference: earlier-ledger AMM snapshot (chosen) vs. reading the parent ledger directly vs. a time-weighted reference; and whether BookStep may write the corridor SLE when the corridor did not fill.

Should the corridor also quote when the AMM is not the best non-corridor source (i.e. peg to the best of AMM and CLOB)? v1 pegs only to the AMM; a best-CLOB peg is future work with manipulation concerns.
Level definition in multi-path payments: one corridor level per Flow iteration (like AMM offers) vs. the model's spot-step levels.
Precision and storage type of the accumulator indices (model: 10^18 fixed point in arbitrary precision; xrpld: Number / 128-bit / STNumber?).
Exit fee while the AMM is unusable (model: waived when missing, empty or frozen) and whether an LP could empty the AMM to free providers from fees.
Issuer transfer fees (TransferRate) on exit fees and claims; frozen fee-pool pseudo-account lines.
Per-ledger fill caps per commitment (MaxPerLedger) as additional manipulation protection.
Whether ineligible commitments (MinRate not met) should count toward MAX_COMMITMENTS_PER_LEVEL (model: they do; a griefing vector mitigated by MinCommit and reserves).
biggestRisk: Payment-engine complexity and consensus risk: a second synthetic liquidity source inside BookStep, plus hold-awareness in every funding path.
excludedFromConsensus: TG Intelligence / Titan Ghost proprietary logic
